questions.question: _________ is NOT appointed by the President of India?

options.text: A judge of a High court

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Advocate General.**__

__
 
• **The Governor **__of each State shall appoint a person who is qualified to be appointed as a Judge of a High Court to be the Advocate General for the State.
 
• The authority and function of the Advocate General are also specified in the Constitution of India under **Article 165 and 177. **

**The duties of Advocate General for the State include:**

__
 
• to give advice to the government of the state upon legal matters.
 
• to perform duties of other legal charter assigned to him by the governor.
 
• discharge the functions conferred to him under the constitution.

questions.question: Which two nations co-chaired the 6th Annual Defence Dialogue in Bengaluru in February 2026?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**India and France.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh and French Minister Ms. Catherine Vautrin co-chaired the 6th India-France Annual Defence Dialogue in Bengaluru on February 17, 2026.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Agreement Renewal:** The two nations renewed their **defence cooperation agreement** for another **10 years**, reinforcing their long-term strategic partnership.
 
• **Missile Manufacturing:** An MoU was signed between **Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL)** and **Safran** (France) to manufacture **Hammer missiles** in India.
 
• **Reciprocal Deployment:** For the first time, both countries announced the **reciprocal deployment of officers** at the Indian Army and French Land Forces establishments.
 
• **Exercise Shakti:** The ministers appreciated the conversion of the bilateral army exercise 'Shakti' from a biennial to an **annual event**.
 
• **Strategic Alignment:** The dialogue focused on co-development and co-production of equipment, specifically in the field of **niche technology** and maritime security in the Indian Ocean Region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **About Hammer Missile__**

 
• The **Hammer (Highly Agile Modular Munition Extended Range)** is a precision-guided stand-off weapon used by the Rafale fighter jets.
 
• The indigenous manufacturing of these missiles under the 'Make in India' initiative will significantly boost the Indian Air Force's offensive capabilities.

questions.question: In which state has the Sambar deer been recorded at high altitudes of over 3,000 meters for the first time in the Gamgul Wildlife Sanctuary?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Himachal Pradesh.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **The Wildlife Wing of the Himachal Pradesh Forest Department documented Sambar deer at high altitudes in the Chamba district via camera traps.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Discovery:** Sambar deer, usually found below 2,000m, were recorded at elevations exceeding 2,500m in **Kalatop–Khajjiar** and 3,000m in **Gamgul** Wildlife Sanctuaries.
 
• **Significance:** This is a first-of-its-kind record for the species in these high-altitude protected areas, published in the **Zoological Survey of India** (Feb 2026).
 
• **Ecological Shift:** Three species—Sambar, Musk deer, and Barking deer—are now co-occurring in the same landscape, which is unusual due to their different habitat preferences.
 
• **Conservation Status:** The Sambar deer is listed as **'Vulnerable'** on the IUCN Red List and is protected under **Schedule III** of the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Sambar Deer (Rusa unicolor)__

 __
 
• It is the largest deer species in South Asia and a vital prey base for large carnivores like leopards and tigers.
 
 
 
• Chamba District Sanctuaries__
 __
 
• The district is home to several key protected areas including **Kugti**, **Tundah**, and **Sechu Tuan Nala**.
 
 
 
• Climate Change Impact__
 
 
• Scientists suggest that shifting wildlife patterns to higher altitudes may be a response to climate change or habitat fragmentation in lower regions.

questions.question: Virupaksha Temple is located in ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hampi.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Virupaksha Temple**__

 __
 
• It is located at **Hampi in Karnataka.**
 
• It has been declared a **UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1986** under Cultural Heritage.
 
• It was built under the rule of **Deva Raya-II **(1424–1446 AD) of the Vijayanagara empire.
 
• The temple is dedicated to **Lord Shiva.**
 
• It is situated on the **banks of the Tungabhadra river.**
 
• It was made in the** Dravidian Style of temple making.**
 
 

**​** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/df8eb9543ac6ce871487ffd92958225393b552cfe279effbc8fd0552c3aefc45.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **Hampi**__

 __
 
• **​**It is also known as Pampa Kshetra, Kishkindha kshetra, and Bhaskara kshetra.
 
• It is the 14th-century **capital of the Vijayanagar Empire.**
 
• It is located in the** Tungabhadra basin** in Bellary District, **Karnataka.**
 
• Famous temples in Hampi are the **Virupaksha temple, Krishna temple, Achyutaraya temple, Vitthala temple, Hemakuta hill monuments, and Hazara Rama temple.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Shore Temple**__

 __
 
• ​It is located in **Mahabalipuram, Tamil Nadu.**
 
• It is classified as a **UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1984.**
 
• The construction of the Shore temple was started by the **Pallava ruler Narasimhavarman II.**
 
 
 
• Brihadeshwar Temple (1010 AD)__
 __
 
• It is at the Tanjore, Tamilnadu.
 
• It was based on the Dravidian Style of Temple Architecture.
 
• It was built by Raja Raja Chola-I of the Chola Dynasty.
 
 
 
• Lingaraj Temple (11th century AD)__
 
 
• It is situated in Bhubaneshwar, Odisha.
 
• It is based on the Nagara Style Temple Architecture.
 
• It was a patron architecture of the Kalinga Dynasty.
 
• It was built by King Jajati Keshari.

questions.question: The 16th edition of Exercise Vajra Prahar commenced between which two nations at Bakloh, Himachal Pradesh in February 2026?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**India and United States.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__** 

__
 
• **The 16th edition of the bilateral India-US Special Forces Exercise Vajra Prahar commenced on 24 February 2026 at the Special Forces Training School, Bakloh, Himachal Pradesh.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

• **Green Berets:**

• Specialize in counter-terrorism, direct action missions, and foreign internal defence.
 
 
 
• **Interoperability:**
 
 
• Refers to the ability of military forces from different nations to operate together effectively.
 
• Includes compatibility in communication systems, operational planning, and tactical execution.

questions.question: Which team created history by winning its maiden Ranji Trophy title in the 2025–26 season after 67 years of participation?

• **Historic Win:** Jammu & Kashmir (J&K) scripted history by clinching their **first-ever Ranji Trophy title** in the 2025–26 season.
 
• **The Final:** They defeated the heavyweights **Karnataka** in the final held at the KSCA Rajnagar Stadium, Hubballi, on 28 February 2026.
 
• **Significance:** This victory ended a 67-year wait for the Union Territory since they first began participating in India's premier domestic red-ball tournament.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Highlights__**

• **Naming:** It is named after **Kumar Shri Ranjitsinhji** (Jam Sahib of Nawanagar), the first Indian to play international cricket.

questions.question: Who became the first Indian woman to win gold in javelin at the Asian Games 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Annu Rani**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Annu Rani** became the **first Indian woman to win a gold medal in javelin throw** at the **Asian Games 2025**. This marked a historic achievement for India in athletics.
 
• She achieved this feat with a remarkable throw that surpassed her competitors, showcasing her exceptional talent and dedication to the sport.
 
• Annu Rani has consistently been one of India's top-performing javelin throwers, having previously represented the country in multiple international events, including the **World Championships** and the **Olympics**.
 
• Her gold medal win at the Asian Games 2025 is a testament to her perseverance and the growing strength of Indian women athletes in track and field events.
 
• This achievement not only brought glory to India but also inspired countless young athletes to pursue javelin throw and athletics as a career.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Annu Rani's Career Highlights:**

 
 
• Annu Rani hails from **Meerut, Uttar Pradesh**, and has been a pioneer in Indian women's javelin throw.
 
• She holds the **national record** in javelin throw, with a throw of **63.24 meters**, achieved at the Federation Cup in 2021.
 
• Annu has represented India in **two World Athletics Championships**, making her one of the few Indian women to do so.
 
 
 
• **Javelin Throw in India:**
 
 
• Javelin throw has gained significant attention in India, especially after **Neeraj Chopra's** historic gold medal at the **Tokyo Olympics 2020**.
 
• India has seen a surge in young talent taking up the sport, with improved training facilities and support from organizations like the **Athletics Federation of India (AFI)**.
 
 
 
• **Asian Games:**
 
 
• The **Asian Games**, also known as the **Asiad**, is a continental multi-sport event held every four years among athletes from all over Asia.
 
• India has been a consistent participant in the Asian Games since its inception in **1951**.
 
• Track and field events have traditionally been strong areas for India, with athletes bringing home multiple medals over the years.
 
 
 
• **Other Indian Women in Athletics:**
 
 
• Indian women athletes like **PT Usha**, **Hima Das**, and **Dutee Chand** have also brought laurels to the country in international events.
 
• Their achievements have paved the way for future generations of women in sports.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other Options Explained:**

 
 
• **Kamalpreet Kaur**: She is a prominent Indian discus thrower who gained recognition for her performance at the Tokyo Olympics 2020 but has no record in javelin throw.
 
• **Seema Antil**: Known for her achievements in discus throw, Seema has been a veteran athlete but not associated with javelin throw.
 
• **Shalini Sharma**: She is not a recognized name in the field of javelin throw or athletics at the international level.
 
 
 
• **India's Focus on Athletics:**
 
 
• The Indian government, through initiatives like **Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS)**, has been providing financial and infrastructural support to athletes.
 
• Improved coaching, exposure to international competitions, and better facilities have contributed to India's growing success in athletics.

questions.question: Where did Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw inaugurate the nation’s pioneering 3nm chip design centres in May 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Noida and Bengaluru**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Union Minister **Ashwini Vaishnaw**, in May 2025, inaugurated India’s first **3nm chip design centres** in **Noida** and **Bengaluru**.
 
• The **3nm technology** is a breakthrough in semiconductor chip manufacturing, offering higher efficiency, reduced power consumption, and better performance compared to its predecessors like 5nm and 7nm technologies.
 
• **Noida** is a growing hub for technology and innovation, hosting several IT and electronic design companies, which makes it a strategic location for such a facility.
 
• **Bengaluru**, known as the **Silicon Valley of India**, is home to numerous tech companies and startups, making it an ideal choice for fostering semiconductor innovation.
 
• This initiative aligns with the Government of India’s **Make in India** and **Digital India** missions, aimed at boosting domestic manufacturing and technological self-reliance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **3nm Technology:**

 
 
• The **3nm (nanometer)** technology refers to the size of transistors on a chip. Smaller transistors allow for more transistors to fit on a chip, enhancing computational power and efficiency.
 
• Compared to **5nm chips**, 3nm chips consume up to **30% less power** while providing **15% better performance**.
 
• This technology is critical for applications in **AI, 5G, IoT, and high-performance computing**.
 
 
 
• **Noida as a Technology Hub:**
 
 
• Noida has emerged as a major IT and electronics manufacturing hub in India.
 
• It hosts several leading companies such as **Samsung, HCL, and Oppo**, contributing significantly to India's electronics ecosystem.
 
• The establishment of a 3nm chip design centre enhances its position in the global semiconductor value chain.
 
 
 
• **Bengaluru’s Role in Tech Innovation:**
 
 
• Bengaluru is renowned for its contributions to **software development, R&D, and electronics design**.
 
• It is home to institutions like **Indian Institute of Science (IISc)** and many tech startups, fostering innovation in cutting-edge technologies.
 
• The city plays a pivotal role in India's semiconductor ambitions, providing a skilled workforce and infrastructure.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives in Semiconductor Sector:**
 
 
• The Government of India launched the **Semicon India Programme**, with an outlay of **₹76,000 crore**, to boost semiconductor manufacturing and design in the country.
 
• It aims to make India a global hub for electronics manufacturing and reduce dependency on imports.
 
• Incentives under the scheme include support for **R&D, design, and manufacturing** infrastructure.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Global Semiconductor Industry:**

 
 
• The global semiconductor market is projected to reach **$1 trillion by 2030**, driven by rising demand for smart devices and connected technologies.
 
• Countries like **USA, Taiwan, South Korea, and China** dominate the semiconductor manufacturing space.
 
• India’s initiatives in the sector aim to establish it as a significant player in the global supply chain.
 
 
 
• **Applications of 3nm Chips:**
 
 
• 3nm chips are used in advanced applications such as **AI processors, autonomous vehicles, quantum computing, and high-speed networking**.
 
• They are integral to devices like **smartphones, laptops, and medical equipment**, offering enhanced capabilities and reduced energy consumption.

questions.question: In 2025, which company has partnered with the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) to restore heritage water bodies?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bisleri**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bisleri**, a leading packaged drinking water company in India, has partnered with the **Archaeological Survey of India (ASI)** in 2025 to restore heritage water bodies across the country.
 
• The initiative is aimed at **reviving traditional water conservation systems** that were historically significant and played a key role in maintaining water availability.
 
• This partnership focuses on **restoration and rejuvenation of ancient stepwells, ponds, and other water bodies** situated at heritage sites under the protection of ASI.
 
• The collaboration aligns with the Indian government’s emphasis on **cultural preservation** and sustainable water resource management.
 
• Under this initiative, Bisleri has pledged to use its expertise and resources to ensure the **scientific and eco-friendly restoration** of these water bodies, while also raising awareness about their historical and environmental significance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Archaeological Survey of India (ASI):**

 
 
• The ASI, under the Ministry of Culture, is responsible for the **protection and preservation of India’s cultural heritage**, including monuments, archaeological sites, and remains of national importance.
 
• It was established in **1861** by Alexander Cunningham and has since played a vital role in safeguarding India’s rich historical legacy.
 
• As of now, ASI protects and maintains over **3,600 monuments**, including ancient water structures.
 
 
 
• **Heritage Water Bodies:**
 
 
• These include traditional water storage systems such as **stepwells, kunds, baolis, and lakes**, which were constructed to meet water needs in historic times.
 
• Many of these structures, apart from serving as water sources, were architectural marvels and had **religious and cultural significance**.
 
• The restoration of these water bodies is crucial for addressing **water scarcity** issues and promoting heritage tourism.
 
 
 
• **About Bisleri:**
 
 
• Founded in **1969**, Bisleri is one of India’s most recognized brands in the **packaged drinking water industry**.
 
• The company is known for its focus on sustainability and has initiated various **CSR activities** related to water conservation.
 
• Its **‘Bottles for Change’ campaign** is a notable initiative aimed at recycling plastic waste and promoting environmental awareness.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives for Water Conservation:**
 
 
• Programs like **Jal Shakti Abhiyan** and **Atal Bhujal Yojana** have been launched to address water conservation and management issues in India.
 
• These programs focus on **rainwater harvesting**, rejuvenation of traditional water bodies, and groundwater recharge.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Restoration of heritage water bodies helps in **combating water scarcity** and promotes environmental sustainability.
 
• It also contributes to **heritage tourism**, creating awareness about India’s rich cultural and architectural legacy.
 
• Partnerships between private entities like Bisleri and public institutions like ASI exemplify the importance of **public-private collaboration** in addressing pressing environmental and heritage conservation challenges.
 
• The initiative aligns with global efforts toward achieving the **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**, particularly SDG 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation) and SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities).

• **Musical Legacy:** Geeta Patnaik was an accomplished **A-grade artist** for All India Radio (AIR) and Doordarshan. She was celebrated for her mastery over **Sugam Sangeet** (light music) and Odissi traditional songs.
 
• **Career Highlights:** She lent her voice to several hit Odia films and was a contemporary of legendary singers like Akshaya Mohanty and Prafulla Kar.
 
• **Early Life:** Born in **Cuttack**, the cultural capital of Odisha, she began her musical journey at a young age and became a household name in the 1970s and 80s.
 
• **Recognition:** Over her decades-long career, she received numerous state-level accolades, including the **Odisha Sangeet Natak Akademi Award** for her immense contribution to the state's musical heritage.
 
• **Impact:** Her passing is considered the end of an era for the "Golden Age" of Odia music, with many political leaders and members of the film fraternity paying their final respects in Bhubaneswar.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Note on Odisha's Music__**

 
• **Odissi Sangeet:** A classical music tradition of Odisha that dates back over 2,000 years, distinct from Hindustani and Carnatic styles.
 
• **Sugam Sangeet:** A popular genre in the state that blends classical ragas with easy-to-understand lyrics, a field where Geeta Patnaik was a dominant figure.

questions.question: With which country did India secure a $131 million deal in May 2025 to acquire 'HawkEye 360’s cutting-edge surveillance technology to advance its maritime defense infrastructure?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**United States of America**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **May 2025**, India secured a deal worth about **$131 million** with the **United States of America** to acquire advanced **HawkEye 360 surveillance technology**.
 
• **HawkEye 360** is a U.S.-based company that specializes in **radio frequency (RF) geospatial intelligence** using satellite constellations.
 
• The technology helps detect and track **radio frequency signals** emitted by ships, communication devices, and radar systems even when vessels attempt to hide their location.
 
• The system strengthens India’s **maritime domain awareness** and supports monitoring of the **Indian Ocean Region (IOR)**.
 
• This acquisition contributes to enhancing India’s **maritime defense infrastructure**, improving surveillance against threats such as **illegal fishing**, **smuggling**, and **unauthorized naval activity**.
 
• ***Hence, the correct option is 4.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **HawkEye 360**

 
 
• A **U.S.-based satellite analytics company** headquartered in **Virginia**.
 
• Uses clusters of satellites to collect **radio frequency (RF) data** from across the globe.
 
 
 
• **Maritime Domain Awareness (MDA)**
 
 
• Refers to the effective understanding of all activities occurring in the **maritime environment**.
 
• Important for monitoring **shipping routes**, **naval operations**, and **illegal maritime activities**.
 
 
 
• **India–US Defence Cooperation**
 
 
• India and the United States have strengthened defence ties through agreements such as **LEMOA**, **COMCASA**, and **BECA**.
 
• These agreements facilitate **logistics support**, **secure communications**, and **geospatial intelligence sharing**.

questions.question: In which two languages were the updated editions of the Constitution of India released by C. P. Radhakrishnan on International Mother Language Day 2026?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tamil and Gujarati.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **The Vice-President of India released the updated editions of the Constitution of India in Tamil and Gujarati along with the 8th Edition of the Legal Glossary (English–Hindi) on 21 February 2026.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **The updated versions of the Constitution were released in Tamil and Gujarati on the occasion of International Mother Language Day (21 February 2026).**
 
• The event was held at the Vice President’s Enclave in New Delhi to promote linguistic inclusivity and constitutional awareness.
 
• The initiative aims to make the Constitution accessible in regional languages, strengthening democratic participation.
 
• The 8th Edition of the Legal Glossary (English–Hindi) was also launched to simplify legal terminology for students, lawmakers, judiciary, researchers, and policymakers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **International Mother Language Day**__

 __
 
• Observed annually on 21 February.
 
• Promotes linguistic and cultural diversity worldwide.
 
• Commemorates the 1952 language movement in East Pakistan to protect the Bengali language.
 
 
 
• **Legal Glossary (English–Hindi)**__
 __
 
• The 8th Edition was released in 2026.
 
• Uses simplified Hindi terminology to enhance legal understanding.
 
• Designed to assist lawmakers, judicial officers, translators, and students.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Translations Initiative**__
 
 
• The Constitution has been translated into several regional languages including Bodo, Dogri, Santhali, and Nepali.
 
• Promotes accessibility of the foundational legal document of India.
 
• Supports multilingual governance and inclusive democracy.

questions.question: The largest freshwater lake in the country is __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Wular Lake**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Wular Lake**, located in Jammu and Kashmir, is the largest freshwater lake in India.
 
• The lake spans an area of approximately **189 square kilometers** and is fed primarily by the Jhelum River.
 
• It plays a significant role in maintaining the hydrological balance of the Kashmir valley and acts as a natural flood reservoir.
 
• Wular Lake is recognized as a **Ramsar Wetland** and is of international ecological importance.
 
• The lake supports a rich diversity of aquatic life, making it vital for fisheries, agriculture, and water resources in the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sambhar Lake**

 
 
• It is India's largest inland saltwater lake, located in Rajasthan.
 
• The lake is known for its high salt production and is a key source of salt for the country.
 
• Sambhar Lake is an important ecological site, supporting migratory birds like flamingos and pelicans.
 
 
 
• **Loktak Lake**
 
 
• Loktak Lake is the largest freshwater lake in northeastern India, located in Manipur.
 
• It is famous for its floating islands, known as **phumdis**, and is home to the Keibul Lamjao National Park, the only floating national park in the world.
 
• The lake is a lifeline for the local community, supporting agriculture, fishing, and hydropower generation.
 
 
 
• **Vembanad Lake**
 
 
• Vembanad Lake is the longest lake in India and the largest lake in Kerala.
 
• It is a significant part of Kerala's backwaters and is known for its tourism and houseboat activities.
 
• The lake is also crucial for fishing and supports a rich diversity of flora and fauna.

questions.question: Which Indian leader spoke at a special session in 2025 on “Environment, COP-30 and Global Health”?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Narendra Modi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Prime Minister Narendra Modi**, a globally recognized leader, has been actively involved in addressing significant global challenges like **environmental sustainability**, **climate change**, and **public health**.
 
• In 2025, during a special session on **“Environment, COP-30, and Global Health”**, he emphasized India’s pivotal role in achieving sustainable development and tackling climate-related issues.
 
• The session was part of the preparations for the **30th Conference of the Parties (COP-30)**, a critical event under the **United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)**. This event highlights global efforts to combat climate change.
 
• As a proponent of green energy and climate action, PM Modi has launched key initiatives such as the **International Solar Alliance (ISA)** and has been a strong advocate for the use of renewable energy sources.
 
• His leadership in promoting the **Mission LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment)** initiative has gained global recognition, focusing on sustainable living and climate-conscious behaviors. *Hence, this makes Narendra Modi the correct answer.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Conference of the Parties (COP):**

 
 
• **COP** is an annual meeting under the **UNFCCC** where global leaders discuss and negotiate actions to combat **climate change**.
 
• The **COP-30**, scheduled to be held in **2025**, will focus on implementing the **Paris Agreement** and achieving net-zero carbon emissions by 2050.
 
 
 
• **India’s Role in Climate Action:**
 
 
• India is a **significant contributor** to global climate efforts, with ambitious goals like achieving **50% renewable energy capacity** by 2030.
 
• Under PM Modi’s leadership, India is advocating for **global equity** in climate responsibility, emphasizing that developed nations should take greater accountability.
 
• **Example:** India is pioneering efforts in **solar energy** and has launched the **Green Hydrogen Mission** to reduce carbon emissions.
 
 
 
• **Global Health and Environment:**
 
 
• The integration of **health and environment** policies is critical to addressing challenges like **climate-induced diseases** and ensuring the well-being of future generations.
 
• India has also been actively involved in promoting **universal health coverage** and addressing the health impacts of environmental degradation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Initiatives by Narendra Modi:**

 
 
• **International Solar Alliance (ISA):** Launched by India and France during COP-21 in 2015 to promote **solar energy** adoption globally.
 
• **Mission LiFE:** A movement introduced to encourage sustainable lifestyle practices and climate-conscious behaviors.
 
• **National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC):** Includes missions like **National Solar Mission** and **National Mission for Enhanced Energy Efficiency** to combat climate change.
 
 
 
• **Global Leadership:**
 
 
• PM Modi’s leadership at global forums like the **G20** and **UN** has been instrumental in shaping international climate policies.
 
• He has consistently advocated for **climate justice**, urging developed countries to contribute more towards climate finance.

questions.question: The salary and allowance of the Prime Minister of India is determined by the __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Parliament__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Salaries and Allowances of Minister Act, 1952 basically deal with the salaries and allowances of the Council of Ministers.
 
 
• On the basis of this Act, these salaries & allowances are determined by the Parliament__.
 
 

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Parliament__: 

 __
 
• The parliamentary system of government is the executive government branch of which has the indirect or any direct support of the parliament.
 
• This direct or indirect support is generally shown by a vote of confidence.
 
• The relationship between the legislature and the executive branch in any parliamentary system is called responsible government. 
 
 
 
• Council of Ministers__: 
 
 
• Under PSA, we may see the Council of Ministers which is headed by the honorable Prime Minister to provide advice to the President to maintained his necessary work accordingly.
 
• The Prime Minister is appointed by the President, who also appoints the governor of states, other ministers after taking advice from the Prime Minister.
 
• The Council of Ministers is also responsible to the Lok Sabha. 
 
• Article 74 of the Constitution of India provides for a Council of Ministers.
